title: AIRC frames and HTTPS bodies
description: JSON Schema for every AIRC frame (docs/airc-spec.md §4, §19, §21, §22, §3.4.6) and HTTPS-only body (§3.4). The root validates any frame by its `t`; `$defs` holds one entry per frame and body, plus the records and primitives they share. Frames keep `additionalProperties: true` throughout, because §3.2 says unknown fields MUST be ignored. Where a frame has two faces (`msg`), both are defined (`msgWire`, `msgClient`). Spec section references are in each description.

id.description: §4.2: a message id, or the id it answers (`re`): 1 to 128 of [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. UUIDv4 recommended.

mediaType.description: §4.2: a MIME type with optional parameters and no control characters; refused otherwise like a bad id.

sha256hex.description: SHA-256 as exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits (§22 `bin_sha256`, §12.2 `token_hash`).

kid.description: §9.1: key id, the first 8 hex digits of SHA-256 over the raw 32-byte public key.

base64url.description: base64url without padding (RFC 4648 §5), as in challenge ids and passport layers.

sigString.description: §9.2: `alg:kid:base64(signature)`. The grammar names only `ed25519`; the alg token is left open because §9.2 says a verifier admits any alg on its allowlist; `none` is never valid.

signatures.description: §9.2: `hdr.sig` is one sigstring or a list of them.

pin.description: §12.1: the first 128 bits of SHA-256 over a raw public key, base62, left-padded with 0 to 22 characters.

passportToken.description: §12.2: at least 128 bits from a CSPRNG in base62, 22 to 64 characters.

realm.description: a realm name: a DNS host (§2.1 `host`), as in `via`, `hello.realm`, `welcome.realm`.

uriAddress.description: §2.1 network form with the scheme: `airc://authority/path[#fragment]`; the only form on the wire (§2.3). A trailing `/` names a namespace; `airc://R/` the realm. At most 1024 octets.

networkAddress.description: §2.3 `//R/p`, the URI form without its scheme; `bound` names and link `bind_to` use it.

localAddress.description: §2.3 local forms a client may write: `ns/name` or `name`, resolved by the local server.

clientAddress.description: §2.3: any form a client may write in `from`, `to`, `as`, `peer`, `scope`: URI, network or local.

pattern.description: §2.7: `*`, or a network-form address whose authority may be `*`, whose segments may be `*`, whose last segment may be `**`, with an optional trailing `/`.

bindName.description: §4.3: a name relative to the realm (`alice/`, `bob/research`, `carol/*`) or absolute; `*`/`**` as in §2.7.

boundName.description: §4.3: an accepted absolute pattern, network form `//R/…` or URI form.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; fractional allowed where the field is `num`.

ttl.description: §4.2: seconds after `ts` the message stays deliverable; default 86400. The spec sets no fixed upper bound (a receiver refuses a ttl over its maximum, 7 days unless configured, §9.3).

ackCode.description: §14.1 ack codes, plus `challenge` (§11.6: a failed ack that carries `challenges`).

errorCode.description: §14.2 `error` frame codes. Open: over HTTPS a server may use codes of its own, and §3.4.4/§3.4.5 add registration and membership codes; the known values are listed as examples.

features.description: §4.1 / §3.4.1: optional features, open list; known values in examples.

segment.description: §2.1 one address segment (a workspace or channel name).

hdr.description: §4.2 extension headers, relayed untouched except as noted. Values are strings or objects, except `sig`, which §9.2 lets be a list of sigstrings. Named headers: §9 `sig`; §11.4 notice headers; §19.9 peer-key headers; §20.2 front-door headers. §6.7 `airc-receipt`: a comma-separated list of receipt types the sender asks for.

airc-link.description: §11.4: the link id of a control or notice.

airc-peer.description: §11.4 notice: the other party's endpoint key.

airc-passport.description: §11.4 notice: on a redemption notice, the passport id.

airc-passport-pins.description: §11.4 notice: the passport's pins joined by `.`.

airc-peer-ik.description: §19.9: the acting endpoint's identity key, passed in the notice.

airc-peer-sig.description: §19.9: the acting endpoint's signature over the control.

airc-peer-control.description: §19.9: the signed fields of a link control, for the endpoint to check.

airc-directory.description: §20.2: the listed agents' URIs separated by single spaces.

airc-echo-of.description: §20.2: marks an automatic reply; a front door does not answer it.

a.description: §11.1: endpoint key, namespace reference or realm. `*` is the local marker of a §12.7 key refusal (`origin.reject_key`), never sent to another server.

expires.description: §11.1: null or a time after which the link has no effect.

origin.description: §11.1 / §12.6 / §12.7 / §12.10: how the link came to be.

opt_out_of.description: §12.7: the group link this record opts out of.

pins.description: §12.7: the pins of the passport that made the link.

chain.description: §12.10: the delegation layers, `{realm, id, pin}` each.

answered.description: §12.9: a pending offer answered by a link with another id or scope.

challenge.description: §11.6 one challenge alternative in a `challenges` list.

url.description: login/oauth: where the user logs in.

need.description: email/sms: the server needs the address first.

sent.description: email/sms: a code was sent; answer with `code`.

proof.description: §11.6: the answer to a challenge, in a `link` offer and in `body.proof` of the control.

contact.description: §11.6: `{"email"?, "phone"?}` given up front with an offer.

authEntry.description: §12.2 / §12.4: one authorizing key and its signature over the passport's terms.

passportAuth.description: §12.6 `body.passport_auth` of a grant: the signed terms and the signatures; §12.10 adds `kind`, `delegates`, `rules`, `layers` for a delegated passport.

bind_to.description: §12.4: a pattern, or empty when none. Allowed null as well as the empty string because the canonical string writes an absent value as empty.

linkControlBody.description: §11.4: the body (JSON text) of an `application/airc-link+json` message.

e2e.description: §19.9: the acting endpoint's identity key and, optionally, its signature.

redemption.description: §12.5: the redeemer's value, copied into the grant.

passport.description: §12.9 step 2: an accept carries the passport.

passportControlBody.description: §12.5 / §12.10: the body of an `application/airc-passport+json` message to `airc://R/_passport`.

oneOf.description: §12.10 closing: a delegate revokes a layer it issued.

passportRecord.description: §12.2 the issuer-side record; `passported` returns it without `token_hash`.

auth.description: one entry per authorizing key, in pin order.

offer.description: §12.9: the offer hash this passport answers.

e2eKeys.description: §19.2 the key record; published with `keys op=publish` or `POST /airc/v0/keys`, fetched verbatim.

sig.description: ed25519 by `ik` over the §19.2 canonical string.

require.description: §19.7: the endpoint accepts only encrypted messages.

e2eEnvelope.description: §19.5 the body of an `application/airc-e2e+json` message; §19.7: servers check this shape.

v.description: 1: `ct` holds the ciphertext; 2: the binary section does (§19.5).

ct.description: ciphertext with tag, at least 16 bytes (v 1 only).

bin.description: v 2: the inner binary section's length.

fileBody.description: §22 the body of an `application/airc-file+json` message; the section holds the file.

name.description: a file name, not a path.

kind.description: §13: open list; the defined kinds are the examples.

profileRecord.description: §21.1 the profile record (also `POST /airc/v0/profile`'s body and `GET`'s response); `{"endpoint","delete":true}` removes it (§21.1), `{"endpoint","close":true}` closes the channel (§21.4).

icon.description: at most 32 bytes of UTF-8 (the schema can check characters only), no whitespace.

image.description: a `data:` URI of type image/png, image/webp or image/jpeg, base64, at most 24 KB decoded; a server MAY return a boolean on GET.

directoryEntry.description: §20.2: a directory entry a workspace adds or hides.

hello.description: §4.1 `hello`, from the connecting side; first frame of a stream connection (§3.3).

ts.description: peer, signed: Unix seconds when the hello was made.

nonce.description: peer: random, at least 12 bytes of entropy, hex or base64. §4.1 asks for ≥12 bytes of entropy, which a schema cannot check.

ns.description: client: namespace claim; servers MUST ignore it unless configured (tests only).

welcome.description: §4.1 `welcome`, from the accepting side; §3.4.6: the first WebSocket message, with `push`.

ns.description: client face (required there): namespaces this connection may act for (§5); empty = anonymous.

sig.description: peer face: signature over the welcome (§9.4).

msg.description: §4.2 `msg`, address form unconstrained: the union of `msgWire` (peer face) and `msgClient` (client face). `bin` and `bin_sha256` come together (§22).

from.description: origin endpoint; any form here, see msgWire/msgClient.

ts.description: origin time, Unix seconds (fractional allowed); required on the peer face.

re.description: the full id of the message this answers.

via.description: realms traversed; set by servers (§6.5); at most 8 hops (§15).

bin.description: §22: length of the binary section after the line.

msgWire.description: §4.2 + §2.3: a `msg` on the wire (peer face, inbox, WebSocket pushes, notices): URI-form `from` and `to`, `ts` required.

msgClient.description: §4.2 + §2.3: a `msg` as a client may send it (stream client face, `POST /airc/v0/send`, WebSocket `send`): local forms allowed, `ts` optional (a server MAY set it).

ack.description: §4.4 `ack`: exactly one per accepted `msg`; §11.6 adds `challenges`; §3.4.6 adds `rid` on the socket.

by.description: URI of the resolver that produced the status.

challenges.description: §11.6: alternatives, any one suffices; with code `challenge`.

rid.description: §3.4.6: the client's request id, repeated in the reply.

bind.description: §4.3 `bind` (client face). Over HTTPS the body may omit `t` (§3.4.2): see `bindRequest`.

names.description: §4.3: names relative to the realm; `[]` releases (§4.3.1).

bindRequest.description: §3.4.2 the body of `POST /airc/v0/bind`: the `bind` frame's fields, `t` optional.

names.description: §4.3: names relative to the realm; `[]` releases (§4.3.1).

ping.description: §4.5 `ping`; `n` is optional and echoed (untyped in the spec; the example uses an integer). §3.4.6: `rid` on the socket; the server's keep-alive is `{"t":"ping"}`.

as.description: the acting endpoint (local form allowed); all ops but `list` (and `list` on a hosted realm).

expires.description: offer: lifetime in seconds, or `30d`/`12h`/`45m`/`2w`; absent: the link does not expire.

id.description: accept/decline/revoke: the link id; offer: optional, chosen by a signing client.

expires_at.description: offer: the absolute expiry the client signed.

sig.description: the acting endpoint's identity-key signature over the control (§19.9), bare base64.

token.description: accept: the passport token the accepting client signed (§12.9).

auth.description: accept: signatures over the §12.4 canonical string.

key.description: revoke/unreject: a pin to refuse, or stop refusing (§12.7).

closed.description: revoke with `key`: the links the refusal closed.

kept.description: revoke with `key`: links site policy keeps (must-accept).

delivery.description: ack status of the control message sent to the other side.

as.description: the acting endpoint; for `redeem` possibly a namespace (trailing `/`).

scope.description: new/key-add/key-remove: endpoint, namespace (trailing `/`) or realm; default `as`.

token.description: new (required): the token the client generated (§12.2).

expires_at.description: new (required): the absolute expiry the client signed.

to.description: new: the pattern the redeemer must match (`bind_to`).

link_ttl.description: new: lifetime of created links, seconds.

for_offer.description: new: a pending offer's link id (§12.9).

offer.description: new: the offer hash the client signed.

auth.description: new: signatures over the terms (§12.4); may be empty.

key.description: key-add/key-remove: a public key to entitle.

and_links.description: revoke: also revoke every link the passport created.

passport.description: new/revoke: the record without the token hash.

code.description: redeem: the ack code; on failure.

error.description: §4.8 `error`, sent before closing a stream connection; §3.4 the body of a non-200 HTTPS response; §3.4.6 a WebSocket reply with `rid`. A 409 `name_held` body also carries `error`, `name`, `idle`, `suggest` (§4.3.1): see `nameHeldError`. `code` on the stream (§4.8); a 409 body on the HTTPS binding carries it as `error` (§3.4.2).
§3.4.2: a 409 name_held/channel_taken body carries its code here

nameHeldError.description: §4.3.1: the HTTP 409 body of a refused bind: `{"error":"name_held","name":<pattern>,"idle":<s>,"suggest":<name>}`; `t` is not stated there.

scope.description: the namespaces the subscriber sees, or `all` for an administrator.

keys.description: §19.3 `keys` (stream client face): publish or get an end-to-end key record.

endpoint.description: get: the endpoint, in any realm.

profile.description: §21.1 / §21.2 `profile` (stream client face): `op` publish (with `record`), get (with `endpoint`) or status (with `statuses`). Without `op` it is the profile record itself (§21.1 `{"t":"profile","endpoint":…}`).

displaced.description: §4.3.1 / §3.4.6 `displaced`: another session took these names over.

send.description: §3.4.6 `send` (client → server over the WebSocket): one `msg` in `msg`.

acks.description: §3.4.6 `acks`: a list of acks over the WebSocket.

inbox.description: §3.4.2 the `GET /airc/v0/inbox` response: queued wire-form messages, oldest first; §4.3.1 `displaced`. §3.4.6: `{"t":"inbox"}` alone over the WebSocket means more is waiting.

kids.description: the realm's signing key ids (protected by TLS only).

did.description: §3.4.1 / §24: the realm's DID, when it serves a DID document.

ackList.description: §3.4.2 the body of `POST /airc/v0/ack`: a list of ack frames.

pub.description: the raw 32-byte ed25519 public key, base64.

recovery.description: adds a recovery code to the response (§3.4.5).

code.description: a join or recovery code (§3.4.5 grammar).

workspaceOp.description: §3.4.5 the body of `POST /airc/v0/workspace`, by `op`. `front` (§20.1 names a hosted realm's `front` action; its fields are not in the §3.4.5 table) is admitted loosely.

expires.description: at most 7 days for a plain code.

workspace.description: §3.4.4 / §3.4.5 / §20.3 the `workspace` response: registration and join (`realm`, `ns`, `kid`, `uri`, …), `GET /airc/v0/workspace` (`keys`, `joins`, `recovery`, front-door fields; a channel key sees `realm`, `ns`, `channel` only), and the `join-code` op (`ok`, `id`, `code`, `kind`). Other op responses (`{"ok":true,…}`, `t` unstated): `workspaceOpResult`.

temporary.description: §3.4.4: a `tmp-` name that expires after 1 idle day.

recovery.description: a new recovery code (registration with `recovery`, join with a recovery code), or on GET whether one exists.

kind.description: join-code: `channel` or `enroll` for a channel/enrollment code.

workspaceOpResult.description: §3.4.5 the response of a `POST /airc/v0/workspace` op other than `join-code`.

skill.description: §21.1 a skill: the shape of an A2A Agent Card skill.

multikey.description: §24: multibase base58-btc Multikey (ed25519 z6Mk…, X25519 z6LS…).

didDocument.description: §24 a realm's (24.1) or endpoint's (24.2) DID document: a mirror of the DNS record or the key record.

receiptBody.description: §6.7 the body of a receipt reply (type application/airc-receipt+json).
